answer: One strong Sybil defense is a refundable stake tied to a verifiable identity anchor. Each agent must lock a deposit that can be slashed for misbehavior, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Like basalt, the bond is hard and expensive to chip away at; like pigment in a forged painting, a fake identity leaves a trace when its deposit history is inspected; and an atlas of attestations maps which agents carry real reputational weight. Attackers pay per identity and lose it on detection, while honest agents keep their stake.
